title: Prioritization Canvas for Commitment Credit & Marketplace Offset Requests
creator: Lena Patel
description: Create a reproducible prioritization canvas and intake flow for customer requests related to commitments, invoicing exceptions, crediting, and marketplace offsets. The canvas will standardize information capture, define SLA thresholds, map decision owners, and provide an escalation matrix for legal/finance/ops. Primary goal is to reduce decision lag and inconsistent crediting across deals while preserving auditability for enterprise contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form fields defined and piloted with Sales and Finance
SLA tiers (Urgent / Standard / Low) and routing rules documented
Decision matrix mapping owners (PM, Finance, Legal, Sales Ops) for common scenarios
Audit trail requirements and required artifacts list (commitment docs, invoices, Marketplace txn details) produced
Pilot run with two enterprise customers and metrics captured: time-to-decision, approvals, reversal rate
out_of_scope: Negotiating new pricing tiers or creating new legal contract templates. Implementation of billing engine changes; this ticket covers intake and decisioning only.
comments: 2026-03-01 Lena Patel: Initial ticket created after cross-functional intake workshop with Sales and Finance. Observed inconsistent responses and missing data fields in current emails/Sheets process.

2026-03-03 Marco Ruiz: Drafted intake form prototype (Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-prioritization-canvas). Added fields for commitment ID, invoice #, Marketplace transaction ID, requested offset amount, and reason code.
2026-03-04 Priya Anand (Finance): Suggest adding 'approved discount' and 'effective date' fields; flagged need for GL mapping stub for downstream accounting feeds.
2026-03-05 Legal review (Y. Martinez): Will require 'authorization evidence' for credits > $50k and retention of correspondence for 7 years. Added as requirement.

2026-03-06 Marco Ruiz: Mapped SLA tiers: Urgent = 48h, Standard = 7d, Low = 21d. Routing rules attached. Trade-off: aggressive SLAs increase review load—proposal to use auto-approval for low-risk marketplace offsets under $500 when audit artifacts present.
2026-03-07 Leah Kim (Sales Ops): Piloting intake with two AE teams next week; will surface real-world missing fields and customer communications templates.

2026-03-08 Engineering note (ENG-34567): Need a webhook endpoint and metadata contract if we want to move from manual Sheets to an automated queue. Estimate: 3 points for a minimal intake webhook + basic validation.

2026-03-09 Marco Ruiz: Updated decision matrix and escalation ladder. GitHub draft for automation spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-intake/pull/42. Preparing pilot comms and success metrics (time-to-decision, approval rate, rollback count).

2026-03-10 Lena Patel: PM review — recommended to proceed with pilot and collect metrics for two weeks before proposing org-wide rollout. Next step: align on dashboard events with Observability (console-2026.04).
rollout_plan: Week 1: Pilot intake form with Sales Ops and Finance for two active enterprise deals
Week 2: Collect metrics and feedback; iterate fields and SLA thresholds
Week 3: Implement minimal webhook and validation with Eng (ENG-34567) for automated queueing
Week 4: Expand pilot to Marketplace ops and finalize escalation lifecycles; prepare runbook for handoff to Ops
